name: S. Shankar Sastry
title: Professor; EMBER Center Faculty Lead
researchAreas: Safe adaptive and game-theoretic robot control
fitReason: Current EMBER research connects CS-based robot learning, generative models and agile physical execution. A focused contribution to policy representation, sim-to-real evaluation or humanoid learning would be a strong topical fit, subject to an actual project and supervisor.

physicalEvidence.summary: HITTER’s September 2025 full revision, listed by EMBER at ICRA 2026, combines planning with a PPO-trained whole-body policy deployed on Unitree G1. It reports 24 successful returns from 26 thrown balls and autonomous human/robot rallies, with the work explicitly performed at Berkeley’s FHL Vive Center. Ball and base sensing use external motion capture. LeVERB separately demonstrates real learned low-level execution, but replays latent instructions generated in simulation; it does not demonstrate a live vision-language feedback loop on hardware.

shortVisit.summary: Current EMBER-listed PhD student Dvij Kalaria explicitly invites undergraduate/master’s research collaborators for VLA, humanoid and table-tennis projects and says visiting students are welcome. His personal page identifies Sastry as adviser. This is a useful member-level inquiry lead, not a faculty-issued 2027 or eight-week offer; zero short-visit points are retained until PI-level scope is established.

unknowns: Official EECS profile confirms current Professor, while the current EMBER people page names him Faculty Lead and lists the student behind the inquiry lead. His linked older personal homepage returns 404; the faculty directory remains a verified professional contact source.

The visitor invitation is undated and the student page retains future-tense May 2026 internship wording. The center independently verifies current membership, but the invitation’s availability, PI approval, exact host, duration and summer 2027 applicability need confirmation.

HITTER’s hardware evidence is directly tied to the current Berkeley center and group, but shared-center affiliation does not guarantee equipment access for a visitor. Its controlled-environment sensing, fixed hitting plane and limited spin handling matter; the reported 26-ball test is not a universal performance guarantee.

LeVERB’s quantitative benchmark is simulated; hardware uses open-loop latent-instruction replay with a learned low-level controller. Do not relabel this as fully closed-loop real-world VLA execution. DreamControl-v2’s separate author list omits Sastry and is not credited to him.

Reuse Berkeley’s saved VSR audit: graduate students outside the UC system with a bachelor’s degree have a 30-day to one-year in-person route, subject to faculty/department approval, funding evidence and immigration review. Its current non-prorated VSR service fee is separate from other costs and needs 2027 rechecking. Institutional compatibility does not confirm lab intake or a remote appointment.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
